subject: Targeted exemption policy proposal for model variant unwind
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Targeted exemption policy proposal for model variant unwind

Team —

As we prepare the variant consolidation next quarter, I want to propose a short-lived, targeted exemption policy we can use for customers with complex integrations (eg, Atlas Health) where a full migration in the initial wave would break production. High-level ask: can we agree on a standard intake, approval guardrails, and comm windows so Customer Success and Sales have predictable expectations?

Key proposal (attached: exemption_template.xlsx + proposed-waves.csv):
- Eligibility: customers with pinned model versions, embedded KV cache dependencies, or documented SLA-critical latencies.
- Duration: max 8 weeks per exemption unless Product approves extension (formal review).
- Controls: rate-limited traffic routing to legacy variant, automated audit logs, and a routing shim flag for emergency rollback.
- Communication: standardized customer email template + internal ops playbook.

Specific asks from each team:
- Product (Karthik): feedback on technical controls and acceptable duration.
- Ops/Serving (Ben): feasibility of rate limits and routing shims; rough SLO delta.
- CS/Ops (Marissa): operational overhead and comm cadence for customers.
- PM (Priyom): approval gate and decision authority for extensions.

Timing: we need to finalize the policy and comm templates by Oct 29 to include in the customer wave planning doc.

Appreciate quick reads — flag any non-starters or must-haves.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: exemption_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: proposed-waves.csv (text/csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeted exemption policy proposal for model variant unwind

Kim — thanks for drafting this. A few operational clarifications from my side: 

1) Intake: we should require a CS-run readiness checklist + a short tech impact note from Solutions Engineering before Ops invests time. That will prevent vague asks.

2) Duration: 8 weeks is reasonable for most customers, but for multi-region regulated customers (Atlas) we should add a mandatory risk review with Security if they request extension beyond 4 weeks.

3) Communications: CS will need a one-page FAQ for customers and an internal triage matrix (who to call at 3am if the shim fails).

I can draft the FAQ and triage matrix if folks agree on the core policy. Also — will customers on Dedicated capacity need different rules? That likely needs a parallel flow.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeted exemption policy proposal for model variant unwind

Kim / team —

Thanks, this is a good start. A couple of technical points to lock before we finalize: 

- Routing shim: we can support a flag to route traffic to legacy variant, but we need to scope how the KV cache is handled (prefix-only vs full-state). For some customers, prefix-only will be insufficient. That affects whether an exemption can be non-disruptive.

- Observability: Ops needs explicit metrics to detect drift between variants (error rate, avg latency, token-level divergence). Can Ben confirm which metrics we can guarantee from the serving runtime within an exemption window?

- Extension authority: Product can approve one 4-week extension for corner cases; anything beyond that must route to a cross-functional review (PM + Eng + CS + Security). We should bake this into the intake template.

If this sounds reasonable I can update the intake template with a short tech-impact checklist.

-Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeted exemption policy proposal for model variant unwind

All —

We can support a routing shim and rate-limiting per-customer, but a few guardrails:
- Implementing a full-state KV handoff for the shim is non-trivial and will add ~2 weeks to the engineering work per major customer. Prefix-only is quick but comes with compatibility risk.
- Observability: runtime can emit latency + error-rate + token-diff sampling. I suggest we add a "divergence" signal that triggers an auto-escalation to on-call if above threshold.
- SLO delta: expect a small latency bump (~10-25ms median) and slight variability under heavy load; we should surface this to CS in the intake.

Operational suggestion: schedule exemptions in two-week waves (small batch of customers per wave) rather than one-offs — easier to staff and reduces blast radius. Proposed waves attached.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Targeted exemption policy proposal for model variant unwind

Thanks everyone — useful input. Quick summary and next steps (action items):

- Intake: Priyom to produce a one-click intake form (linked to HS-12345) + mandatory SE tech-impact note. Due: Oct 26.
- Tech controls: Karthik and Ben to define KV handling options and required runtime metrics; Ben to confirm divergence signal implementation plan. Due: Oct 27.
- CS comms: Marissa to draft customer FAQ + internal triage matrix. Due: Oct 28.
- Approval: Product (Kim) sign-off on policy; Product may grant single 4-week extension. Any extension beyond that triggers cross-functional review.
- Wave scheduling: Ops (Ben) recommends two-week waves; Priyom to slot eligible customers (start Nov 8 wave).

@Alex (Atlas) — looping you in so you see the policy we plan to offer for customers with complex integrations. If you'd like a pre-review of Atlas's intake, can you share the current pinned variant details and any KV assumptions?

I'll spin up a 30-minute sync for Oct 28 to finalize templates — calendar invite to follow.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
